subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: For the remaining CORE.md and directory read failures, should OpenClaw fix only the scheduled producer/prompt, or change the generic read tool so directory paths return listings instead of EISDIR failures?
rationale: Both approaches could reduce the symptom, but changing read-tool directory semantics affects the model-facing tool contract while the producer has not been isolated.

options.title: Producer-first repair
options.body: Reproduce the scheduled run on current main and fix the producer or prompt that emits stale paths while keeping read-tool semantics unchanged unless proven inadequate.

options.title: Read-tool contract change
options.body: Make read-on-directory return a listing, but treat that as a model-facing behavior change requiring explicit tests and maintainer approval.

options.title: Close after live non-repro
options.body: If a current release soak shows no repeated read errors or RSS growth, close with stability proof instead of changing code.

recommendation.title: Producer-first repair
recommendation.body: Reproduce the scheduled run on current main and fix the producer or prompt that emits stale paths while keeping read-tool semantics unchanged unless proven inadequate.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent read-tool and heartbeat scheduler work makes this the best available routing owner for the producer-versus-tool contract choice.
